pattern.summary: 8 questions, attempt any 5, each carries 20 marks. About half are computations (salary, house property, capital gains, other sources, total income); the rest are provisions and short notes.
pattern.caution: Tax rates, limits and rules change every year and these papers use older assessment years. The notes give the method; for exact limits use the figures in your IGNOU course material or those given in the question.

choosing: A salary computation (allowances, perquisites, gratuity or pension) appears in every paper — master one full format and you have a safe 20 marks.
House property annual value, capital gains with indexation, and income from other sources are the other regular computations.
Theory questions repeat: residential status, casual and agricultural income, clubbing, set-off of losses, e-filing, and section 54 exemptions.
numerical: Write the name of the head and the assessment year at the top, then a two-column format (Particulars / ₹).
Mark each item Taxable / Exempt with the section number in brackets — examiners give marks for the reasoning.
Show a working note for every exemption calculation (HRA, gratuity, commuted pension): list the three limits and pick the least.
Use the limits stated in the question; if none, state the figure you assumed.

topics.name: Income from Salaries
topics.summary: Computation of taxable salary: allowances (HRA, entertainment), perquisites (house, car, servants), gratuity, pension, leave encashment, provident funds.
points: Salary includes basic pay, DA, bonus, commission, fees, allowances, perquisites, retirement benefits, advance salary (taxed when received).

Allowances: fully taxable (DA, city compensatory, overtime, servant, medical); partly exempt (HRA, children education, hostel); entertainment allowance — deduction u/s 16(ii) only for government employees.

HRA exemption (Sec 10(13A)) = least of: actual HRA received; rent paid − 10% of salary; 50% of salary in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai (40% elsewhere). Salary = basic + DA (forming part of retirement benefits) + commission at a fixed % of turnover.

Perquisites: rent-free house (a % of salary depending on city population), car (depends on engine capacity and private/official use), servants (sweeper, gardener, cook — actual cost), free gas, electricity and water.

Gratuity (Sec 10(10)) — covered by the Gratuity Act: least of actual, 15/26 × last month's salary × completed years (part over 6 months counts as a year), statutory limit. Not covered: least of actual, ½ × average salary of last 10 months × completed years, limit.
Commuted pension (Sec 10(10A)): government employees — fully exempt; others — ⅓ of full commuted value exempt if gratuity also received, ½ if not. Uncommuted pension is fully taxable.
Leave encashment on retirement: least of actual, 10 months' average salary, cash equivalent of unavailed leave (max 30 days per year of service), statutory limit.
Provident funds: statutory (fully exempt), recognised (employer's contribution exempt up to 12% of salary; interest up to 9.5%), unrecognised, public provident fund.
Deductions from gross salary: standard deduction, entertainment allowance (government), professional tax (Sec 16(iii)).
method: List basic, DA, bonus, commission → add taxable allowances (show HRA working) → add perquisites → gross salary.
Less deductions u/s 16 → income under the head Salaries.
For retirement benefits, compute each exemption in a separate working note.
formula: HRA exempt = min(HRA, Rent − 10% of salary, 50%/40% of salary)
Commuted pension exempt = ⅓ (with gratuity) or ½ (without) of full commuted value
mistakes: Using basic pay only for HRA 'salary' — add DA that forms part of retirement benefits and commission on turnover.
Not rounding service years (over 6 months = full year) for covered gratuity.

topics.name: Basic Concepts, Casual & Agricultural Income
topics.summary: Previous year and assessment year, person and assessee, GTI vs total income, casual income, agricultural income and partial integration, exempt incomes.
points: Income of the previous year (PY) is taxed in the assessment year (AY) that follows it. Exceptions (taxed in the same year): non-resident shipping companies, persons leaving India, bodies formed for a short duration, assets transferred to avoid tax, discontinued business.
Person (Sec 2(31)): individual, HUF, company, firm, AOP/BOI, local authority, artificial juridical person. Assessee: person by whom tax is payable; assessee in default fails to pay or deduct tax.
Gross total income = total of the five heads after clubbing and set-off. Total income = GTI − deductions under Chapter VI-A.
Casual income: lottery, crossword puzzles, races, card games, gambling, TV game shows — taxed at a flat 30% with no deduction of expenses or basic exemption.

Agricultural income (Sec 10(1)) is exempt: rent or revenue from agricultural land in India, income from agriculture, farm buildings. Partly agricultural: tea (40% business income), coffee (25%), rubber (35%).
Partial integration: when a non-corporate assessee has agricultural income above ₹5,000 and non-agricultural income above the basic exemption limit, agricultural income is used to fix the tax rate.
Exempt incomes u/s 10: agricultural income, share of profit from a firm, HUF receipts, gratuity/commuted pension (limits), leave encashment (limits), scholarships, PPF interest, etc.
Capital receipts are generally not taxable; revenue receipts are taxable unless exempt.
method: Agricultural income from land: sale proceeds − cultivation expenses (seeds, fertiliser, labour, depreciation, electricity).
formula: Total income = GTI − Chapter VI-A deductions

topics.name: Capital Gains & Exemptions (54, 54B, 54F)
topics.summary: Capital asset, short- and long-term gains, computation with indexation, exemptions u/s 54, 54B, 54F, Capital Gains Account Scheme.
points: Capital asset: property of any kind held by the assessee — excludes stock-in-trade, personal effects (except jewellery, paintings), rural agricultural land, certain bonds.
Short-term vs long-term: depends on holding period (e.g. listed shares 12 months, immovable property 24 months, other assets 36 months — as per the course material).
Transfer includes sale, exchange, relinquishment, compulsory acquisition.
LTCG = full value of consideration − transfer expenses − indexed cost of acquisition − indexed cost of improvement. For assets bought before 1-4-2001, cost may be taken as FMV on 1-4-2001.
Sec 54: LTCG on a residential house exempt if invested in another residential house (bought 1 year before or 2 years after, or built within 3 years).
Sec 54B: gains on agricultural land invested in new agricultural land within 2 years.
Sec 54F: LTCG on any other asset exempt proportionately if net consideration is invested in a residential house.
Capital Gains Account Scheme, 1988: unutilised amount deposited in a bank before the return due date is treated as invested.
method: Full value of consideration − transfer expenses = net consideration.
Indexed cost = cost × CII of year of transfer ÷ CII of year of acquisition (or 2001-02).
Capital gain = net consideration − indexed cost; then subtract exemption (amount invested + CGAS deposit, up to the gain).
mistakes: Forgetting the CGAS deposit when computing the exemption.

topics.name: Income from House Property
topics.summary: Chargeability (Sec 22), annual value, let-out and self-occupied property, deductions u/s 24, interest on borrowed capital.
points: Sec 22: annual value of buildings or land appurtenant, owned by the assessee, not used for own business or profession.
Gross annual value: expected rent (higher of municipal value and fair rent, but not more than standard rent) compared with actual rent received — the higher is GAV.
Net annual value = GAV − municipal taxes actually paid by the owner.
Self-occupied property: annual value nil (for one or two houses); interest deduction limited.
Deductions u/s 24: (a) standard deduction 30% of NAV; (b) interest on borrowed capital (pre-construction interest in 5 equal instalments).
Part let-out, part self-occupied, part used for own profession: split the property and compute each part separately; the professional-use part is not taxed under this head.
method: Expected rent = max(municipal value, fair rent), capped at standard rent.
NAV = GAV − municipal tax paid by owner.
formula: Income = NAV − 30% of NAV − interest u/s 24(b)
mistakes: Deducting municipal tax paid by the tenant.

topics.name: Deductions (80C, 80D, 80G) & Total Income
topics.summary: Computing total income across heads, and Chapter VI-A deductions — 80C, 80D, 80G, political donations.
points: Compute income under each head, add (after clubbing and set-off) → GTI → less deductions → total income.
80C: LIC premium, provident fund, PPF, NSC, ELSS, tuition fees, home-loan principal — up to the overall limit.
80D: medical insurance premium for self/family and parents (higher limit for senior citizens); must not be paid in cash (except preventive health check-up).
80G: donations to funds and charities — 100% or 50%, with or without a qualifying limit (e.g. PM National Relief Fund 100% without limit).
80GGC: donations to political parties — 100%, not in cash.
Casual winnings, LTCG and STCG u/s 111A are taxed at special rates — Chapter VI-A deductions are not allowed against them.
Income from growing mushrooms is not agricultural income; share of profit from a firm is exempt.
method: Head-wise schedule: Salary, House Property, PGBP, Capital Gains, Other Sources → GTI.
Less Chapter VI-A deductions (show each with its section) → total income.
mistakes: Allowing 80C against capital gains or lottery income.

topics.name: Residential Status & Incidence of Tax
topics.summary: Residential status of individuals, HUF and companies; ordinarily resident vs not ordinarily resident; income deemed to accrue in India.
points: Individual is resident if in India for 182 days or more in the PY, or 60 days in the PY and 365 days in the 4 preceding years (the 60-day rule is replaced by 182 for Indian citizens leaving for employment and for visiting NRIs, with conditions).
Resident and ordinarily resident (ROR) vs resident but not ordinarily resident (RNOR): RNOR if non-resident in 9 of 10 preceding years or in India 729 days or less in 7 preceding years.
HUF is resident if control and management is wholly or partly in India. Company is resident if Indian or its place of effective management is in India.
Incidence: ROR — global income; RNOR — Indian income plus foreign income from a business controlled from India; non-resident — only income received or accrued/deemed to accrue in India.
Income deemed to accrue in India (Sec 9): business connection, property or asset in India, salary for services in India, interest, royalty, fees for technical services paid by residents.
method: Count days of stay in the PY and preceding years; apply the basic conditions, then the additional conditions.
mistakes: Counting the day of departure and arrival wrongly — both days count as days in India.

topics.name: Income from Other Sources
topics.summary: Chargeable incomes, casual winnings, dividends, interest on securities, composite letting, bond washing, allowed deductions.
points: Residual head: dividends, interest on securities and bank deposits, casual winnings, gifts above limits, composite letting of building with machinery, director's sitting fees, family pension, ground rent.
Winnings from lottery, races, card games: grossed up if received net of TDS (net ÷ 70%) and taxed at 30%; losses from such games cannot be set off.
Dividends: taxable in the shareholder's hands (from AY 2021-22); dividend from a co-operative society is taxable.
Deductions allowed: collection charges, interest on borrowed money, depreciation and repairs on let machinery/building, standard deduction on family pension.
Bond washing (Sec 94): selling securities just before interest is due and buying them back after — the interest is taxed in the seller's hands.
Exempt: share of HUF income, agricultural income, salary of an MLA is taxed under Other Sources (not Salaries).
method: List each receipt: taxable/exempt with section → deduct allowed expenses → income from other sources.
mistakes: Allowing expenses on lottery tickets against winnings.

topics.name: Clubbing of Income & Set-off of Losses
topics.summary: When another person's income is clubbed; set-off and carry forward of business, capital, speculative and lottery losses.
points: Clubbing (Secs 60–64): transfer of income without transfer of asset; revocable transfer of assets; remuneration of spouse from a concern where the individual has substantial interest (unless due to technical skill); assets transferred to spouse or son's wife without adequate consideration; income of a minor child (clubbed with the parent with the higher income; exemption up to ₹1,500 per child; not clubbed if from the child's own skill or if the child is disabled).
Set-off within the same head first, then against other heads.
Speculative business loss: only against speculative income; carried forward 4 years.
Short-term capital loss: against STCG or LTCG. Long-term capital loss: only against LTCG. Both carried forward 8 years.
Non-speculative business loss: against any head except salary; carried forward 8 years (only against business income).
Losses from lottery, card games, races: cannot be set off or carried forward.
House property loss: inter-head set-off limited; carried forward 8 years.
topics.frame: Meaning → each rule as a headed point with the section and a one-line example → conclusion.

topics.name: Return Filing, PAN, Assessment & Authorities
topics.summary: e-filing steps and benefits, consequences of late filing, PAN, best judgement assessment, income tax authorities.
points: e-Filing steps: register/log in on the income tax portal with PAN → choose the correct ITR form (e.g. ITR-1 Sahaj for salary, one house property, other sources up to the limit) → fill or use pre-filled data → compute and pay tax → submit → e-verify (Aadhaar OTP, net banking, DSC) within the time allowed.
Benefits: loan and visa proof of income, claim refunds, carry forward losses, avoid penalties, quick processing.
Late filing: late fee u/s 234F, interest u/s 234A, some losses cannot be carried forward, belated return u/s 139(4).
PAN (Sec 139A): 10-character alphanumeric number; required for filing returns and many financial transactions.
Best judgement assessment (Sec 144): when the assessee fails to file a return or comply with notices, the AO assesses to the best of judgement.

Income tax authorities: CBDT, Principal Chief Commissioners/Chief Commissioners, Commissioners (incl. Appeals), Joint/Additional Commissioners, Deputy/Assistant Commissioners, Income Tax Officers, Tax Recovery Officers, Inspectors.
Marginal relief: surcharge limited so that extra tax does not exceed the extra income above the threshold.
topics.frame: Meaning → steps or provisions as headed points → conclusion.

topics.name: Profits & Gains of Business or Profession
topics.summary: Conditions for chargeability, depreciation, Sec 43B, Sec 37(1) general deduction, inadmissible expenses, presumptive tax u/s 44AD.
points: Conditions: business or profession carried on by the assessee during the PY; income is taxed on accrual (mercantile) or cash basis.
Depreciation (Sec 32): block-of-assets, WDV method; asset used for less than 180 days in the year of purchase gets half the rate.

Sec 43B: certain expenses allowed only when actually paid (by the return due date) — taxes and duties, employer's PF/ESI contribution, bonus, commission, interest to banks/financial institutions, leave encashment.
Sec 37(1) general deduction: expenditure wholly and exclusively for business, not capital, not personal — e.g. advertisement, repairs, staff welfare, legal expenses.
Not allowed: income tax, personal expenses, penalties for breaking the law, capital expenditure, cash payments above the limit (Sec 40A(3)), interest/salary to partners beyond Sec 40(b) limits.
Sec 44AD presumptive taxation: eligible small businesses declare profit at 8% of turnover (6% for digital receipts), no books needed.
topics.frame: Section → rules as headed points with examples → conclusion.

topics.name: Assessment of Firms & Partners
topics.summary: Partnership deed, conditions u/s 184, working and non-working partners, interest and remuneration to partners.
points: A firm is assessed as a firm (Sec 184) if there is a written partnership deed, a certified copy is filed with the first return, and partners' individual shares are specified.
Deed contents: names, business, capital, profit-sharing ratio, interest on capital, remuneration to working partners, duration.
Working partner: actively engaged in the business; non-working (sleeping) partner is not.
Sec 40(b): interest to partners allowed up to 12% simple p.a.; remuneration only to working partners within prescribed limits based on book profit.
Partner's share of profit from the firm is exempt (Sec 10(2A)); interest and remuneration are taxed as business income in the partner's hands.
topics.frame: Meaning → conditions/provisions as headed points → conclusion.
